label: Clustering Analysis and Automatic Clustering
topic: Storage and Data Protection: clustering depth, clustering keys, Automatic Clustering and cost

questions.scenario: A fact table named sales_fact has no clustering key. A Data Engineer wants to know how well it is clustered on order_date and region before deciding on a key.
questions.stem: Which statement returns the clustering depth for those two columns?

options.text: SELECT SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_DEPTH('sales_fact', 'order_date, region');
SELECT SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_RATIO('sales_fact', '(order_date, region)') AS depth;
SELECT SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_DEPTH('sales_fact', '(order_date, region)');
SELECT SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_DEPTH('sales_fact');

explanation.correct: For a table without a clustering key the column list is required, and it goes in parentheses. Any columns can be passed, which lets the engineer test a candidate key before defining it.

distractors.A: The column list must be inside parentheses, even for a single column.
distractors.B: SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_RATIO is deprecated, and it returns a ratio from 0 to 100, not the depth.
distractors.D: A table without a clustering key needs the column argument, and omitting it returns an error.

questions.scenario: A table was clustered recently under Snowflake's newer clustering engine. A Data Engineer runs SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION on it and finds that total_constant_partition_count and partition_depth_histogram are missing from the output.

options.text: The table uses Optima Clustering, and the version field of the report shows OPTIMA
The table has more than 2 million micro-partitions, so Snowflake leaves out the histogram for large tables
Automatic Clustering is suspended on the table, so the report leaves these fields empty
The histogram is returned only when a predicate is passed to the function as a third argument

explanation.correct: For tables that use Optima Clustering, total_constant_partition_count and partition_depth_histogram are not available. The version field shows OPTIMA or CLASSIC.

distractors.B: For a table with more than 2 million micro-partitions the results are based on a subset, and total_partition_count reports 2 million. The histogram is still returned.
distractors.C: Suspending Automatic Clustering does not remove fields from the report. The missing fields are specific to Optima Clustering.
distractors.D: The predicate argument belongs to SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_DEPTH, and SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION does not take it.

questions.scenario: An events table of about 30 TB is filtered by a date range and by event_type, which has about 25 distinct values. The column event_ts is a TIMESTAMP_NTZ that is almost unique for every row, and is_test is a Boolean that the queries do not filter on.
questions.stem: Which clustering key does Snowflake's guidance favor?

options.text: CLUSTER BY (event_ts, event_type)
CLUSTER BY (TO_DATE(event_ts), event_type)
CLUSTER BY (is_test, event_type, TO_DATE(event_ts))
CLUSTER BY (event_type, TO_DATE(event_ts))

explanation.correct: A key should order columns from lowest to highest cardinality, and an expression such as TO_DATE reduces the cardinality of a timestamp while keeping its order.

distractors.A: A nearly unique timestamp has very high cardinality, is expensive to maintain, and placed first it weakens clustering on event_type.
distractors.B: This puts the higher-cardinality date before event_type, and a high-cardinality column placed first reduces the effect of clustering on the next one.
distractors.C: A Boolean has too few distinct values to prune well, and the queries do not filter on it.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer clones a clustered 5 TB table for a development team. Weeks later, queries on the clone slow down as new data is loaded. The TABLES view shows AUTO_CLUSTERING_ON = OFF for the clone, and AUTO_CLUSTERING_ON = ON for the source.
questions.stem: What should the Data Engineer do?

options.text: Recreate the clone with CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT, which copies the clustering key and keeps it running
Run ALTER TABLE ... RESUME RECLUSTER on the clone so that Automatic Clustering starts again
Increase the warehouse size used by the loads, so that the data is clustered as it is loaded
Wait for Snowflake to resume Automatic Clustering, which restarts on its own after a clone is used

explanation.correct: A clone keeps the clustering key, but Automatic Clustering is suspended on the clone and must be resumed with ALTER TABLE ... RESUME RECLUSTER.

distractors.A: CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT does not carry the clustering key over, so the key would have to be defined again.
distractors.C: Automatic Clustering is serverless and uses no warehouse, so warehouse size does not cluster the data.
distractors.D: Automatic Clustering stays suspended on a clone until someone resumes it.

questions.scenario: A 20 TB orders table has no clustering key. A manager asks for the estimated initial and maintenance credits to cluster it on order_date and region before approving the change.
questions.stem: Which approach gives the estimate before any key is defined?

options.text: Run SYSTEM$ESTIMATE_AUTOMATIC_CLUSTERING_COSTS('orders', '(order_date, region)') and read the result
Query ACCOUNT_USAGE.AUTOMATIC_CLUSTERING_HISTORY for the table and add up the credits used
Run SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION('orders', '(order_date, region)') and read the cost field in the report
Run SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_RATIO('orders', '(order_date, region)') and convert the ratio into credits

explanation.correct: SYSTEM$ESTIMATE_AUTOMATIC_CLUSTERING_COSTS estimates the cost of clustering a table for the first time, and when possible of maintaining it. It is a best-effort estimate.

distractors.B: AUTOMATIC_CLUSTERING_HISTORY shows credits already used. A table without a key has no clustering history to add up.
distractors.C: The report describes depth, overlap and errors. It has no cost field.
distractors.D: SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_RATIO is deprecated, and it measures how well a table is clustered, not what clustering costs.

questions.scenario: Under Optima Clustering, cost is the uncompressed data ingested times the rate per GB times an overlap factor between 0 and 1, which is the share of ingested data that needs active clustering. A team compares four workloads on clustered tables.
questions.stem: Which workload has the lowest cost under Optima Clustering?

options.text: Nightly UPDATE statements that change the values in the clustering key columns
Loads of late-arriving rows that fall into older date ranges and overlap existing partitions
Append-only loads of new rows into a table clustered by TO_DATE(ingestion_time)
Loads of rows in random key order, so that each load overlaps most existing partitions

explanation.correct: Append-only loads clustered by an ingestion timestamp have an overlap factor near 0, so they cost little or nothing.

distractors.A: Updates that change clustering key values usually have an overlap factor of 1, which is the full rate.
distractors.B: Data that partly overlaps existing partitions has an overlap factor between 0 and 1, so it costs more than append-only loads.
distractors.D: Rows in random key order overlap most existing partitions, so the overlap factor is high and so is the cost.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer reviews how Snowflake stores a large fact table and how queries skip data before proposing a clustering key.
questions.stem: Which THREE statements are correct? (Select THREE.)

options.text: The engineer defines the micro-partition boundaries when the table is created
Each micro-partition keeps the minimum and maximum value of every column
A hybrid table can be given a clustering key to improve its pruning
A micro-partition holds 50 MB to 500 MB of uncompressed data
The value ranges of different micro-partitions can never overlap
A filter that contains a subquery is not used to prune micro-partitions

explanation.correct: Micro-partitions hold 50 MB to 500 MB of uncompressed data and keep the minimum and maximum value of each column, which Snowflake uses for pruning. Snowflake does not prune on a predicate that contains a subquery, even if the subquery returns a constant.

distractors.A: Micro-partitions are formed automatically from the order in which data is inserted or loaded. Nobody defines them up front.
distractors.C: Clustering keys are not supported on hybrid tables, whose data is always ordered by primary key.
distractors.E: Micro-partitions can overlap in their range of values, and the amount of overlap is what clustering depth measures.

questions.scenario: A Data Engineer prepares clustering keys for three tables. One key uses a path inside a VARIANT column, one table is a copy made with CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT, and one table has a text column that shares its first characters across rows.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Changing the clustering key rewrites all existing rows as soon as the statement runs
CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT does not carry the clustering key over to the new table
On Clustering Classic, every character of a text column counts toward the key
A key on a VARIANT column needs a path and a type, such as v:"Data":id::NUMBER
A clustering key can be removed only by dropping and recreating the table

explanation.correct: A CTAS table does not keep the key, so it has to be defined afterward. A key cannot be put directly on a VARIANT column, so a path and a target type are given.

distractors.A: Changing the key does not affect existing rows until Snowflake reclusters the table.
distractors.C: On Clustering Classic only the first 5 bytes of each text column are used, so a key can use a substring that starts after the shared characters.
distractors.E: A key can be altered or dropped at any time with ALTER TABLE ... DROP CLUSTERING KEY.

questions.scenario: A team runs Automatic Clustering on several large tables and reviews how it behaves, what it needs, and how to stop it before documenting the operating procedure.
questions.stem: Which THREE statements are correct? (Select THREE.)

options.text: DML on a table is blocked while Snowflake reclusters the table
Defining a clustering key makes Snowflake start reclustering right away
Automatic Clustering is serverless, so it needs no virtual warehouse
A suspended table still accrues clustering credits, at a lower rate
Changing the key resumes Automatic Clustering if it was suspended
Dropping the clustering key stops all future reclustering on the table

explanation.correct: Automatic Clustering is serverless and uses no warehouse. Changing the key resumes it, and writing LINEAR counts as a change. Dropping the key stops all future reclustering.

distractors.A: DML is not blocked while a table is reclustered.
distractors.B: Defining a key does not start reclustering at once. Snowflake monitors the table and reclusters only when it would benefit.
distractors.D: While Automatic Clustering is suspended there is no automatic reclustering and no clustering credits.
